clue.text: Setter working with a policy to be true to expected form

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over and reshaped into something new

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler and a set rule combine to keep things conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges SETTER plus APOLICY, thirteen letters in all; 'with' just joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conforming to a fixed, conventional image is exactly what a standard expected form looks like.

clue.text: Dish out the wrong cash (with bit missing)

definitions.text: Dish out the wrong cash (with bit missing)

parts.words: Dish out the wrong cash (with bit missing)
parts.note: handing over too little money in change, so a bit is missing from what the customer is owed

explanation.surface: A careless or dishonest cashier gives back too little money.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat someone by giving insufficient change is precisely handing out wrong cash with a bit missing.

clue.text: Even this is seen in Latin set of principles

parts.note: the Latin word et can mean even or also, as well as and
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: A remark that even this word turns up in Latin, viewed as a moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen in Latin' tells you both pieces are Latin words: ET (even, also) and HIC (this).
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral code, a body of principles guiding conduct.

clue.text: Red agents after reform become alienated

indicators.note: after reform means the letters have been reorganised into a new order

explanation.surface: Communist spies, having been reformed, become cut off from their old comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reform' rearranges REDAGENTS; 'become' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged describes someone made distant or hostile, the same as being alienated from others.

clue.text: Emulsion paint matched up for each area

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for matched is read from bottom to top

parts.note: met, as in met a standard, means matched
per means for each

explanation.surface: A paint description: an emulsion priced up for each area to be covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MET into TEM, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made by binding pigment in an emulsion, traditionally egg yolk.

clue.text: It's hard to cage up dog

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read together from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a coop is a cage for poultry

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is difficult to keep a dog shut up in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run HCOOP backwards; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is an informal, affectionate word for a dog.

clue.text: State of Mexico that's running very low?

definitions.meaning: a large northern Mexican state bordering Texas
a tiny dog breed whose short legs keep it running close to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads like a reservoir or supply running out, but it is a playful description of a very small dog scampering about.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a Mexican state and the tiny dog breed named after it, which runs low to the ground.

clue.text: Alkaline liquid does for some polyesters

indicators.note: for some means only part of the following word is used, the letters lying within it

explanation.surface: A note that a caustic solution damages certain synthetic fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' looks like 'ruins', but here 'does' is a link and 'for some' marks the letters inside poLYEsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is a strongly alkaline solution, such as sodium hydroxide, used in cleaning and soap making.

clue.text: Sweetheart's quiet tease

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A lover's gentle, silent teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: JO, a Scots word for a sweetheart (as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'), is crossword staple; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh is to tease someone in a good-humoured way.

clue.text: One should delay seeing the heartless politician or one will get almost nothing

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: A dilemma: delay over an unprincipled politician, or end up with practically nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle H from THE, giving TE; 'almost' trims ZERO to ZER. 'seeing' and 'will get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporizer is someone who stalls or delays to gain time, avoiding a decision.

clue.text: Where the stakes are raised to give better protection

definitions.text: Where the stakes are raised to give better protection

parts.words: Where the stakes are raised to give better protection
parts.note: reads like gambling stakes being raised, but means wooden posts being put up as a defensive barrier

explanation.surface: A gambler raising the stakes to cover a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive enclosure of upright wooden posts, stakes raised for protection.

clue.text: Intuitive feeling when inhaling a joint

indicators.note: inhaling means taking something in, so the letter goes inside the feeling word

parts.note: a hunch is an intuitive feeling

explanation.surface: A gut instinct that comes over someone while smoking a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' in the surface is a cannabis cigarette; as the definition it is a cut of meat or the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunch is the hip and thigh, a joint of the body or a joint of meat such as venison.

clue.text: Jesse and Constant and Leslie and Mark

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant, as in the speed of light
Les is the short form of Leslie
a tick is a mark

explanation.surface: A list of four people, as on a roll-call or law firm's letterhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of names. A jesse is a branched church candlestick modelled on the Tree of Jesse. The first and third 'and' are links; the second gives AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A jesse is a large branched brass candlestick decorated as the genealogical Tree of Jesse.

clue.text: What's sometimes taken after cheese

parts.note: looks like a course or drink following the cheese board, but means the snapshot taken once the subjects have said 'cheese' to smile

explanation.surface: A diner asks what usually follows the cheese course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: People are told to say cheese so they smile, and then the picture is snapped.

clue.text: Bridal gear of tussore worked with gold

indicators.note: worked suggests material being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A bride's outfit made of tussore silk worked with gold thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges TUSSORE into TROUSSE; 'with' just joins on AU. Tussore is a coarse wild silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage.

clue.text: Where one might live in Hull?

definitions.text: Where one might live in Hull?

parts.words: Where one might live in Hull?
parts.note: suggests an address in the English city of Hull, but means living inside a boat's hull

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to find accommodation in the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire; the capital letter hides the hull of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating home has a hull, so its residents literally live in a hull.

clue.text: Hideous art new group starts to put up in gallery

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An ugly art collective's new work is about to be exhibited in a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang a picture is to put it up for display, as galleries do with exhibitions.

clue.text: Cause downfall of party of peacekeepers

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are troops of the United Nations
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A celebration held by United Nations troops brings about someone's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party of peacekeepers' is the United Nations' DO, so UN comes first; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to ruin them or bring about their downfall.

clue.text: Put out of action? Put into it? Open to argument

indicators.note: into it means the second piece goes inside the word just found

parts.note: to disable is to put out of action

explanation.surface: Two questions about putting things out of or into action, ending in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is two questions: the first supplies a word for disabling, the second says the other 'Put' goes inside it, signalled by 'into it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputable can be questioned or contested, so it is open to argument.

clue.text: Son has unfinished model to spray

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a pattern is a model to copy

explanation.surface: A boy with a half-built model kit decides to spray-paint it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims PATTERN to PATTER; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to splash or scatter liquid in drops, which is to spray.

clue.text: Survey of North and South America taken by church

indicators.note: taken by places the following pieces after the church abbreviation, as if collected by it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A church conducts a survey of the whole of the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins N and S; CE, the Church of England, takes them and US in.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count or survey of a population.

clue.text: Tiny amount held in common's no answer

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: something shared is held in common

explanation.surface: A small portion held in common among people gives no answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes A (answer) from SHARED; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or very small piece, as in not a shred of evidence.

clue.text: Such a gem might make them stay

indicators.note: might make says the gem's letters could be rearranged to form the following words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lucky gemstone that might persuade people to remain.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the gem's name rearranges into THEM STAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz prized as a gemstone.

clue.text: Euphoric, speak gently reading out Japanese poem

indicators.note: reading out means the words are spoken, so the sound is what matters

parts.note: euphoric is high, and to speak gently is to coo

explanation.surface: Someone elated softly recites a Japanese verse.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH plus COO, said together, sounds like the poem's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese verse form of seventeen syllables in three lines.

clue.text: Everything, for instance, meeting carnivore retreating fairly speedily

parts.note: all means everything
eg means for example

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the animal word is read in reverse

parts.note: an otter is a meat-eating mammal

explanation.surface: Everything, for example, encounters a predator backing away fairly quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns OTTER into RETTO; 'meeting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking meaning moderately fast, slower than allegro.

clue.text: A person's luck getting a great deal

definitions.meaning: one's fate or portion in life

explanation.definitionFit: Lot means both one's fortune in life and, informally, a large quantity.

clue.text: Bird favouring lakes or hiding from antelopes

indicators.note: hiding from means the word or is concealed, that is taken away from the animals

parts.note: oribis are small African antelopes

explanation.surface: A water bird prefers lakes, or keeps away from antelope herds.
explanation.walkthrough: The oribi is a small African antelope; removing OR from ORIBIS leaves the bird. 'or' looks like a link but is the removed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird found around lakes, marshes and wetlands.

clue.text: Shocked as wagon rumbles ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the rumbling word before the vehicle word

parts.note: thunders means rumbles loudly
a truck is a wagon, especially a railway goods wagon

explanation.surface: Someone stunned as a cart rumbles along in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link, and 'ahead' signals that the rumbling verb comes before the vehicle rather than after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderstruck means astonished or shocked, as if struck by lightning.
